subject: Finly discovery - p95 latency & streaming concurrency
messages:
From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@finly.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-15T17:22:00-07:00
Subject: Intro + discovery notes - Finly

Marissa — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our side so we have aligned expectations before the next call.

Pain points we called out:
- Tail latency: our current provider shows p95 of ~800-1200ms for 1k-token completions during peak times (we're seeing occasional spikes >2s).
- Streaming UX: users complain the first token is delayed and then tokens arrive in large bursts which breaks our client playback. First-byte delay is the dominant complaint.
- Concurrency and throttling: we have concurrent streaming sessions that spike (bursts up to ~120 concurrent streams) and our system gets throttled causing dropped streams.
- Cost predictability: current hybrid approach (hosted + on-prem experiments) has been unpredictable at scale.
- Compliance: SOC 2 evidence and audit logs required for enterprise.

Current stack:
- Prototype uses hosted OpenAI endpoints and a small self-hosted fleet for cost experiments.
- Frontend is a streaming-based chat UX (long-running sessions, multi-turn context ~3k tokens).

Success criteria (what would make this a go):
- Stable streaming UX: first token consistently <200ms, smooth token delivery for long responses.
- p95 request latency target: ideally <350ms for non-streaming generation for our typical prompts (1-1.5k tokens).
- Concurrency: ability to sustain 100+ concurrent streaming sessions without throttling.
- Clear cost/per-token economics and SLA commitments.

Next steps from Finly:
- Share representative sample payloads and peak traffic profiles (I'll attach an exported sample).
- Schedule a technical deep-dive with our infra and ML engineering — prefer tomorrow morning (US/Pacific).

Attaching: finly-requirements.xlsx (sample payloads + traffic profile).

Thanks — Sam
Sam Patel
Head of Product, Finly
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@finly.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-15T19:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro + discovery notes - Finly

Sam — really appreciate the detailed notes and the attachment. Quick recap from our side and proposed plan so everyone's aligned.

Summary of what we heard:
- Primary risk is streaming tail + first-token latency at peak concurrency (you see p95 up to ~1s+).
- Secondary concerns: cost unpredictability and enterprise compliance (SOC 2, audit logs).
- Workload shape: multi-turn chat, ~3k token contexts, bursts up to ~120 concurrent streams, typical response lengths ~500–1k tokens.

Initial success criteria (draft):
- p95 non-streaming generation: <= 350ms (for your representative prompts).
- Streaming first-token: <= 200ms consistently.
- Sustain 100 concurrent streaming sessions with p95 tail <= 800ms (we'll refine during benchmarks).
- Documented unit economics ($/token) for a sustained 30-day estimate and SLA wording for availability and latency regressions.

What Redwood will do next:
1) Aditya and Dev (cc'd) will run a perf plan against a small POC using your sample payloads. We'll validate both hosted and Dedicated configs (request-level and continuous-batching profiles).
2) We'll produce a short perf playbook (what to expect, measurement methodology, acceptance criteria) — see attached "redwood-perf-playbook.pdf" (draft).
3) Schedule: propose 60–90min technical deep-dive with our infra/serving engineer tomorrow Apr 16 at 10am PT. If that works, we'll share a calendar invite with dial-in + prep doc.

Action items for Finly:
- Please confirm the deep-dive time or propose an alternative.
- Share any additional compliance docs we should review (SOC 2 scope, encryption/KMS requirements).
- Confirm which model(s) you'll want to evaluate (open Llama, fine-tuned variant, or a commercial model) — this affects kernel/quantization guidance.

If this all looks right I'll move forward with scheduling the deep-dive and spinning up an initial perf harness.

Thanks — looking forward.

— Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Sam Patel <sam.patel@finly.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-16T08:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro + discovery notes - Finly

Thanks Sam/Marissa — quick technical note ahead of the deep-dive. I'll own the perf runs and baseline data. To make the initial tests meaningful, please: 
- Share 10 representative prompt/response pairs (we only need payloads, no PII).
- Confirm average response token length and max expected tokens per call.
- Tell us if you want to evaluate a single model topology or multiple variants (e.g. open Llama-3 vs a tuned 13B vs hosted commercial model).

Planned test matrix (high level):
- Single-request p95 baseline (no batching), followed by continuous-batching profiles tuned for throughput.
- Streaming benchmarks: measure first-token latency, initial burst behavior, and steady-state per-token latency under sustained concurrency (100 concurrent streams).
- Concurrency ramp tests to identify saturation and fallback points.

Preliminary config suggestions to consider for POC:
- Start with Redwood Hosted to validate latency and streaming UX quickly. If the workload needs consistent sustained throughput, test Redwood Dedicated with reserved GPU pools and KV-cache warming for multi-turn contexts.
- We'll test quantized variants for cost comparisons but will keep a float baseline for latency targets.

Tentative acceptance thresholds (we can refine during measurement):
- p95 non-streaming: <= 350ms
- streaming first-token: <= 200ms
- sustain 100 concurrent streams with p95 tail <= 800ms

I'll bring sample perf logs and a concise checklist to tomorrow's deep-dive.

-Aditya
Aditya Rao

- We'll prioritize streaming UX for the POC.
- I've attached the sample payloads you requested and the traffic shape spreadsheet (finly-requirements.xlsx).
- Model: we'll start with a tuned Llama-3 (13B) and also test your recommended hosted commercial baseline for comparison.
- Compliance: I'll share our SOC 2 scope doc via the Drive link in the next email.
- Proposed POC window: Apr 26–May 3 (we can shift earlier if you have capacity).

I'll accept the invite for Apr 16 10am PT for the technical deep-dive and bring our infra lead. Looking forward to the perf playbook and acceptance criteria so we can sign off internally.

— Sam
